NOT SHOWN, and not estimated:
• MODELLED. DC's FY2024 hundred grown to FY2030 at the prior-law rate implied by the
national model's own counterfactual — basis_national's FY2024 hundred against
tobe2030's FY2030 prior-law total, CBO January 2025 baseline vintage. Derived in
code, never typed. Corroborated by, not derived from, DC's own observed growth of
5.49% on Exhibit 16 FY2022-24. SUPERSESSION HUNTED AND NOT FOUND, 2026-10-29: both
DHCF agency chapters, the FY2026 budget testimony, the FY2026 budget slides and the
June 2025 MCAC budget presentation all stop at the budget year, and the District
publishes its four-year plan at District and fund level rather than as an agency
Medicaid trajectory. Not proved absent — the Executive Summary volume of the FY2026
Proposed budget is unchecked. The national-implied rate stands until then.
• Public-company earnings and dual-plan retention: no DC figure
• The payer lanes are the FY2024 composition rescaled proportionally onto the FY2030
disbursement, which the HR-1 levers have already reduced. Proportional because the
stated assumption is that the shape of the dollar does not move, only its level; no
lane is claimed to absorb more of a lever than another. A lever that falls on one
lane in particular would break that, and would be drawn differently.
• Four of the seven HR-1 tributaries are now derived on District inputs and three
remain absent. Nothing on this panel is allocated from CBO's national score: the
denominators are DHCF's, the dollars are DHCF's, and where a rate is modelled it is
declared as one. The three absent levers are absent for three different reasons, and
each records what would be needed to derive it from District sources.
• Section 71102, the blocked eligibility-and-enrolment rule, is left absent
deliberately. Its effect falls on process rather than on a nameable group, and the
people affected are those who would have enrolled or stayed enrolled under easier
mechanics — a counterfactual, not a row in any District report. A
provision-by-provision mapping of our own would be a modelled step with no source
behind it.
• The residual lane is renamed for the District. Nationally it is a remainder defined
by what CBO scored, which cannot be re-derived from District sources because it is
not a thing. The DC lane carries three named District provisions instead — the LTSS
home equity cap, the legal immigrant eligibility restriction, and retroactive
coverage — and is NOT comparable lane-to-lane with the national residual. None is
sized, so the lane's amount stays absent. The immigrant provision is under a
preliminary injunction and its status is contested.
• The two enrolment levers rest on one modelled step: the share of the expansion
group that does not survive them. It is published as a band with a declared default
inside it, and the default is the rate implied by CBO's own score rather than a
figure of our choosing. THE BAND'S ENDS ARE NOT LIKE-FOR-LIKE WITH ITS DEFAULT: the
default is a share of expansion-group spending, which includes people the requirement
exempts, while the Arkansas and New Hampshire outcomes are coverage loss among those
subject to the requirement. Until the District's exempt share is established the
upper end is an upper bound.
• Provider tax limits and directed payment caps are coupled in the District and are
not coupled in the national model. DC's directed payments are financed by a hospital
provider tax, the tax freeze returns the programme to its FY2025 level in FY2027, and
the phase-down then runs on that reverted base from FY2029. The coupling is now
MODELLED IN SEQUENCE. The two lanes do not double-count because they are not the same
dollar: the tax lever is non-federal FINANCING that will not be collected and leaves
at state government, the directed payment lever is a PAYMENT that will not be made
and leaves at claims. Two stages of one event, drawn where the money actually stops.
• The provider tax lever is published at the NON-FEDERAL level. In the District the
dedicated tax is the non-federal share and it draws federal match, so a dollar of tax
never collected costs more than a dollar of Medicaid. The multiplier is not
established and is declared absent rather than guessed. This is a divergence from the
national treatment, not an application of it.
• Section 71115's rate taper does not reach the District at all. The expansion-state
safe harbour steps down to 3.5 percent by FY2032 and DC's hospital tax is 3 percent
of net patient revenue, below every step including the floor. The District's entire
exposure is the freeze on taxes not imposed as of 4 July 2025. A jurisdiction can be
fully exposed to the section while sitting under every threshold in its schedule.
• The first year of the directed payment phase-down is FY2029, resolved on the rule.
CMS-2449-P states that the phase-down begins with the first rating period starting on
or after 1 January 2028, and DC's rating period is the federal fiscal year, confirmed
on two documents. A period beginning 1 October 2027 starts too early. DHCF's own
budget materials say FY2028, which would make FY2030 the third step and the reduction
$145.56M; the disagreement is recorded rather than averaged, and the model does not
move to meet it.
• The phase-down does not terminate by FY2030. KFF's analysis of the approved
preprints puts 100 percent of the District's hospital directed payment above the new
limit, because the base rate alone already exceeds the Medicare-based ceiling, so the
programme runs down over ten steps and FY2030 at two is partial. Stating the
termination YEAR on District evidence rather than on KFF's conversion needs DC
hospitals' commercial price as a percentage of Medicare, which is not yet acquired.
• No DC service allocation is published and none has been estimated, so the claims
fan is unallocated, as in FY2024.
• The prior-law FY2030 flow holds the FY2024 composition and grows only the level.
Every trunk and lane figure on this panel is that assumption, not a projection: no DC
source projects them. It ignores known shape changes — enrolment growth concentrated
among people aged 65+, dual-eligible capitation rising faster than the rest of the
book, and the District's own FY2026 eligibility reductions.
Absent data is left absent. Filling a gap with a share would produce a modelled figure
wearing a measured figure's clothes.
